The 3D Super-Resolution (SR) Module reconstructs high-resolution volumetric data from low-resolution inputs generated by an Implicit Neural Representation (INR), providing intrinsic denoising and reducing reconstruction artifacts such as ringing and blurring [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the 3D Super-Resolution (SR) module employs the SRNO model, which uses deep learning to learn transformations from low-resolution to high-resolution data. It confirms that the SRNO model possesses intrinsic denoising abilities and produces fewer artifacts such as ringing and blurring compared to other techniques. Furthermore, the text describes the SR module as using a 3D CNN with an Attention Mechanism to improve volume resolution, restoring it close to the original. The claim accurately reflects these details regarding the input (low-resolution from INR), the process (SR module/SRNO), and the outcomes (high-resolution output, denoising, reduced artifacts).
